How much does it cost to run a kettle?

A kettle draws a lot of power, but only for a few minutes. The cost depends on how much water you boil, not on the wattage.

Cost per use
3.9p
About £57.48 a year at 3 minutes per use, 28 uses a week.

Standing charge not included.

Adjust for yours
Ofgem price cap average for 1 Oct – 31 Dec 2026 (standard variable tariff, Direct Debit, England, Scotland & Wales).

About these figures

A typical kettle uses about 3,000 watts (1,800–3,000W depending on the model). Used for 3 minutes per use, 28 uses a week, it costs about 3.9p per use and £57.48 a year at the current price cap rate.

Worth knowing: Cost depends on water boiled, not wattage.

Source for the typical figure: CSE 'What uses watt?' table. See how we calculate.

Ways to cut the cost

  • Boil only the water you need, because a full kettle takes roughly three times as long as one mug's worth.
  • Descale regularly; limescale slows heating.
  • Faster (higher-watt) kettles don't cost more per boil. The energy needed to heat the water is the same.

Questions

How much does it cost to run a kettle per hour?

At 26.32p/kWh, a 3000W model costs about 79p an hour while it's running.

How much does it cost to run a kettle per year?

About £57.48 a year, based on 3 minutes per use, 28 uses a week. Change the sliders above to match how you use yours.

Is the standing charge included?

No. You pay the standing charge every day whether or not the appliance is used, so it isn't part of the cost of running it.

How do I find my kettle's actual power use?

Check the rating label, plug or manual for the wattage, or the energy label for kWh figures. A plug-in energy monitor shows exactly what it uses.
